{{legend0|#808080|No data}} | title = U.S. Representative | before_election = [[Lisa Blunt Rochester]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[Sarah McBride]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) }} The '''2024 United States House of Representatives election in Delaware''' was held on November 5, 2024, to elect a member of the [[United States House of Representatives]] to represent the [[U.S. state|state]] of [[Delaware]] from its {{ushr|DE|AL|D}}. The election coincided with the [[2024 United States presidential election|2024 U.S. presidential election]], [[2024 United States House of Representatives elections|other elections]] to the U.S. House, [[2024 United States Senate elections|elections]] to the [[United States Senate]], and various other [[2024 United States elections|state and local elections]]. Incumbent [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] representative [[Lisa Blunt Rochester]] was first elected in [[2016 United States House of Representatives election in Delaware|2016]] and re-elected in [[2022 United States House of Representatives election in Delaware|2022]] with 55.5% of the vote.{{cite news |title=Delaware First Congressional District Election Results |work=The New York Times |date=November 8, 2022 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2022/11/08/us/elections/results-delaware-us-house-district-1.html |access-date=6 May 2023}} Blunt Rochester declined to seek re-election, instead running [[2024 United States Senate election in Delaware|for the U.S. Senate]].{{Cite news |last1=Mutnick |first1=Ally |last2=Otterbein |first2=Holly |date=June 1, 2023 |title=Rep. Lisa Blunt Rochester to launch run for Delaware Senate seat in June |work=[[POLITICO]] |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2023/06/01/lisa-blunt-rochester-delaware-senate-seat-00099778 |access-date=June 2, 2023 |archive-date=June 8, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230608214450/https://www.politico.com/news/2023/06/01/lisa-blunt-rochester-delaware-senate-seat-00099778 |url-status=live }} The primary election took place on September 10, 2024. [[Sarah McBride]] won the primary election on September 10, 2024, and the general election on November 5, and is the [[List of LGBTQ members of the United States Congress|first openly transgender member of Congress]].{{cite news|url = https://www.nbcnews.com/nbc-out/out-politics-and-policy/sarah-mcbride-first-transgender-congress-delaware-rcna177878|title = Sarah McBride becomes the first out
